status_changes.description: Host header is mandatory in every HTTP/1.1 request
status_changes.rationale: HTTP/1.1 specification (RFC 7230) mandates the Host header for all requests. The LLM Spec Agent confirms this requirement.

status_changes.description: Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding must be present when request has a body
status_changes.rationale: HTTP/1.1 specification requires one of these headers to indicate body length when a body is present. The LLM Spec Agent confirms this.

status_changes.description: POST, PUT, PATCH requests should include Content-Type header with body
status_changes.rationale: While not strictly mandatory by spec, it is a strong convention and best practice. The LLM Spec Agent indicates this as a requirement for proper operation.

status_changes.description: HEAD response must not include a body
status_changes.rationale: HTTP/1.1 specification (RFC 7231) explicitly states that HEAD responses must not contain a body. The LLM Spec Agent confirms this.

status_changes.description: OPTIONS * is a server-level options request where path equals asterisk
status_changes.rationale: This is standard HTTP behavior for origin-form requests to the server. The LLM Spec Agent confirms this interpretation.

status_changes.description: In 3xx redirect responses, Location header is required and contains the redirect target URI
status_changes.rationale: HTTP/1.1 specification (RFC 7231) requires Location header in most 3xx responses. The LLM Spec Agent confirms this.

status_changes.description: Request must precede response in the message exchange cycle
status_changes.rationale: Fundamental HTTP request-response model. The LLM Spec Agent confirms this sequential dependency.

status_changes.description: After receiving 401 Unauthorized, client may retry with Authorization header
status_changes.rationale: Standard HTTP authentication flow. The LLM Spec Agent confirms this transition pattern.

status_changes.description: After receiving 3xx redirect, client typically follows Location header with new request
status_changes.rationale: Standard client behavior for redirects. Trace evidence (Session 3) and spec agent both confirm this pattern.

PATCH.template:
PATCH /path HTTP/1.1
Host: <host>
Content-Type: <mime>
Content-Length: <n>
[User-Agent: <agent>]
[Authorization: <creds>]
[Cookie: <cookie>]
[Connection: keep-alive|close]

<body>
